[00:00] Jordan Ellis: hey everybody thanks for joining, we, uh, we're Jordan from Redwood, with Priya who is our systems engineer, and we'll run through the MSA and DPA items and the dedicated SLA and pricing.
[00:16] Michael Tan: thanks Jordan, sorry a little late on my side, flight delay. quick scope — we just want to make sure data residency and DPA terms line up with our existing vendor framework.
[00:30] Priya Kapoor: thanks Michael, yeah we'll cover that; quick note on the dedicated offering, it's Redwood Dedicated — sometimes in docs we see it abbreviated as Redwood Dedicate, so apologies for any confusion — but it's the reserved GPU capacity with VPC peering and customer keys.
[00:47] Sara Lopez: can you confirm whether the dedicated option supports our KMS setup? we use AWS KMS with external HSM through our key provider.
[00:58] Priya Kapoor: yes, we support customer-managed keys, KMS integrations and in private/on-prem installs we can integrate with your HSM. for hosted Dedicated we typically do KMS endpoint peering or bring-your-own-key model. there are some nuances — e.g., key escrow is not enabled by default — but we can show integration steps in the onboarding playbook.
[01:20] Dr. Alan Greer: clarify retention windows for audit logs — our audit team requires 7 years for certain logs, is that supported?
[01:30] Jordan Ellis: good question, Alan. our default audit retention is 90 days for the standard plan, but for enterprise we have add-on retention packs and archive/export tooling to push logs into your S3 or SIEM for long-term storage. we can add explicit language in the MSA/DPA about retention responsibilities and export timelines.
[01:50] Michael Tan: we'd prefer the vendor to commit to export capability and a clear SLA on export turnaround, not necessarily vendor storage for 7 years.
[02:00] Priya Kapoor: that's doable; technically what we do is automate daily exports to your bucket on schedule and provide integrity checks. turnaround SLA for exports is usually within 24 hours for Dedicated customers, we can put that in the SLA matrix.
[02:20] Speaker 2 (unclear): quick question on SOC 2 — you have SOC 2 Type II, correct?
[02:25] Jordan Ellis: yes we are SOC 2 Type II, and ISO is in process; I'll include the audit pack and certifica — certificate in the docs we send.
[02:36] Sara Lopez: procurement asked about termination for convenience notice and refunds for pre-paid Reserved capacity — can you walk us through typical refund terms?
[02:45] Jordan Ellis: typically reserved capacity is committed for the term — annual or monthly commit options — refunds are limited; we do provide step-downs and pro-rated credits if capacity is turned off early, but large discounts are tied to the term length. we'll send the pricing spreadsheet that shows monthly vs annual commit economics.
[03:03] Michael Tan: so procurement needs the exact clause language to pass legal review. we'll likely redline the MSA and DPA.
[03:10] Jordan Ellis: totally expected. we'll send editable redlines and a tracked-changes packet. Priya, anything to add from SE perspective?
[03:18] Priya Kapoor: yes, from the pilot side: we recommend a four-week pilot on a small dedicated pool — that gives you perf numbers and evals for latency/cost. we can run a baseline with your synthetic workload and give a bench sheet. it also helps with the security review since we'll do a runbook for key rotation, access controls and a short ATO checklist.
[03:40] Dr. Alan Greer: about the pilot, do you need network firewall changes? we prefer IP allow-listing and strict egress controls.
[03:48] Priya Kapoor: we can support static IPs for Dedicated and VPC peering, and will document the firewall rules. a short window of 2–4 maintenance hours may be required for initial peering but otherwise it's steady state.
[04:05] Speaker 1 (Michael or Jordan): there's also the question of model licensing and data handling — will CedarPharma's training data ever be used to fine-tune public models?
[04:12] Jordan Ellis: no — by default customer data is not used to train our public models. we can include contractual language in the DPA that customer prompts and outputs are not used for model training unless explicitly agreed and scoped as a separate engagement.
[04:28] Michael Tan: good, legal wants that explicit.
[04:31] Sara Lopez: on the PO and payment flow: we have a quarterly procurement cycle, if you can get pricing and the MSA out by next Thursday we can aim to approve on 9/3.
[04:41] Jordan Ellis: yes we can hit that. we'll aim to send redlines and the pricing sheet by 2026-08-27.
[04:47] Priya Kapoor: related to SLAs, what availability target are you expecting? we have standard 99.9% SLA for Dedicated with credits, and 99.5% for hosted tiers.
[04:58] Dr. Alan Greer: for production workloads we expect at least 99.9 and a clear escalation path with response times. our security and infra teams require 2-hour incident response for sev-1.
[05:10] Jordan Ellis: we can include a 2-hour initial response commitment in the enterprise SLA for sev-1s with phone escalation. credits are tiered based on minutes of downtime.
[05:21] Michael Tan: ok, please include the escalation matrix — names not required, but titles and phone windows.
[05:26] Priya Kapoor: will do. I'll attach the standard SLA matrix and highlight the Dedicated numbers.
[05:33] Speaker 3 (crosstalk): did someone mention competitor contracts?
[05:36] Jordan Ellis: yes Michael said they're also evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI for some use cases; note that bedrock was mentioned for infra alignment. our differentiator is the Dedicated VPC and the predictable unit economics for inference.
[05:52] Michael Tan: cost is a big factor — our finance team wants the model for cost per thousand tokens under normal and peak loads, especially for the gen and embeddings flows.
[06:03] Priya Kapoor: we'll provide a cost model sheet: tokens-per-request, average token length, baseline latency, and recommended batch settings. that'll be in the pricing appendix.
[06:14] Sara Lopez: procurement also needs insurance and indemnity caps spelled out. do you have standard limits?
[06:20] Jordan Ellis: yes we have standard commercial insurance and can provide certs. indemnity is something we can discuss with legal — typical limits are based on the contract value; we'll add our standard language to the redline.
[06:33] Dr. Alan Greer: one more security note: are there customer-segregated logs for request/response? we need the ability to forensically trace tenant-level activity.
[06:43] Priya Kapoor: yes, tenant-level audit is available; we generate per-tenant request IDs and you can ship logs to your SIEM. we also support trace hooks for the runtime to trace token paths, though that might be sanitized for privacy reasons.
[06:59] Michael Tan: excellent.
[07:03] Jordan Ellis: recap — action items: Jordan will send redlined MSA and DPA and the compliance pack by 8/27; Priya will send the Dedicated pricing spreadsheet and SLA matrix by 8/26; CedarPharma to confirm procurement window and the PO process by 9/3; Dr. Greer to confirm KMS/HSM specifics by 8/31.
[07:22] Sara Lopez: that's right. also please include a sample PO template if you have one.
[07:26] Jordan Ellis: yes, we'll include a sample PO and invoice flow.
[07:30] Priya Kapoor: and we'll set up the pilot kickoff call — propose week of 9/7, we can send an invite after procurement alignment.
[07:38] Michael Tan: sounds good. any other questions?
